cohort: The study included 76,451 women at extreme ages of reproductive life from 23 Sub-Saharan African countries.
finding: The prevalence of stillbirth in Sub-Saharan Africa was 6.18%, with higher odds associated with advanced maternal age, alcohol consumption during pregnancy, cesarean section delivery, rural residence, high community levels of illiteracy, and residing in South sub-Saharan Africa.
mod_finding: Women who underwent cesarean section delivery had higher odds of stillbirth (AOR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.11, 1.37).
